hadith:
Lost Things Picked up by Someone (Luqatah) - Narrated Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani:

A bedouin went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about picking up a lost thing. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Make public announcement about it for one year. Remember the description of its container and the string with which it is tied; and if somebody comes and claims it and describes it correctly, (give it to him); otherwise, utilize it." He said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! What about a lost sheep?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "It is for you, for your brother (i.e. its owner), or for the wolf." He further asked, "What about a lost camel?" On that the face of the Prophet (ﷺ) became red (with anger) and said, "You have nothing to do with it, as it has its feet, its water reserve and can reach places of water and drink, and eat trees."
message: When we align ourselves with Allah and His Messenger, we find ourselves guided by An Noor (The Light), whose illumination dispels the darkness of confusion and wrong action. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) taught us to be honest and truthful in all matters—whether returning lost belongings or fulfilling trusts—let us remember that integrity in our dealings reflects our obedience to Allah and opens our hearts to receive His guidance and mercy.
name:
An Noor - النُّورُ - The Light

The name An Noor originates from the Arabic word 'Noor', which means light. It is associated with the Quranic verse that highlights Allah as the source of light in both the physical and spiritual realms. This name encourages reflection on the guidance and clarity that faith provides to individuals, illuminating their path in life.
verse:
Al-Hashr - The Exile - 59:4

This is because they defied Allah and His Messenger. And whoever defies Allah, then Allah is truly severe in punishment.
